subject: Secure SDLC artifact delivery and redaction clarifications
messages:
From: Alex Garcia <alex@finservco.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finservco.com
Date: 2026-10-28T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Request: SDLC artifacts for SOC2 / SIG review

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. As part of our assessor intake for SOC 2, they asked for a short bundle showing how Redwood handles secure SDLC controls for the services we're evaluating. Specifically they're asking for: 
- 3 representative code-review examples (redacted diffs ok) covering a normal deploy and a hotfix deploy
- CI/CD runner logs for the same runs (redacted usernames acceptable)
- Evidence of ephemeral secret handling and rotation (sample KMS audit lines)
- Change ticket history that maps PR -> ticket -> deploy for a 30-day window

Can you confirm what you can provide and an ETA? We need a link to download the artifacts and a short narrative describing redaction and retention policies to present to the assessor.

Appreciate it—
Alex
Security Lead, FinServCo

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Garcia <alex@finservco.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-29T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SDLC artifacts for SOC2 / SIG review

Alex,

Thanks — we can assemble this. Marissa & Karthik are on the thread; Karthik will produce the redacted CI logs and PR samples, Marissa will pull the change-ticket mapping and the deploy chronicle.

Plan / ETA:
- Today: deliver a manifest describing each artifact and the redaction rules (who, what, why)
- 2026-11-03 EOD: ZIP with 3 redacted code-review samples + CI logs + deploy-ticket CSV + KMS snapshot lines
- 2026-11-06: follow-up note with short narrative for assessor and link to a short screen-share if they want to walk through artifacts

Tell us acceptable redaction level: remove developer identifiers only, or also remove PR titles and branch names? We typically preserve PR ids and timestamps to show traceability.

Jordan Blake
Director, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

On Wed, Oct 28, 2026 at 3:03 PM Alex Garcia <alex@finservco.com> wrote:
> (see above)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Garcia <alex@finservco.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T10:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SDLC artifacts for SOC2 / SIG review

Folks,

Upload is ready for initial review — I've prepared redacted files in the internal staging bucket and attached the manifest. Short notes on redaction approach:
- Code-review samples: developer names and emails were replaced with uid- hashes; PR titles left intact; diffs kept verbatim except for any literal secrets (none present in our commits).
- CI runner logs: all usernames and IP addresses redacted; runner ids and timestamps preserved; sensitive environment lines removed (we keep exit codes and step durations).
- KMS snapshot: we export limited audit lines showing rotation events and which service principal initiated the rotation (redacted to svc-xxxxx).
- Change-ticket mapping: we export ticket id, PR id, deploy timestamp, and approver role (not approver name).

Attachments included (stubs below):
- redacted-code-review-samples.zip (3 PR folders: PR-4521_normal-deploy, PR-4699_hotfix, PR-4730_feature)
- ci-runner-logs-redacted.pdf (compiled step timelines for the three runs)
- deploy-ticket-history.csv (ticket_id, pr_id, deploy_ts, approver_role)
- kms-token-access-snapshot.csv (rotation_ts, key_id, initiating_principal)

Two quick clarifying Qs for Alex: is it acceptable to leave PR ids visible (example: PR-4699)? If you need PR ids removed we can map to an internal index, but that will add 1 business day. Also confirm the 30-day window should be Sep 1–Sep 30 or Sep 15–Oct 15 (we pulled Sep 1–Sep 30 by default).

Karthik
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Garcia <alex@finservco.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-06T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: SDLC artifacts: delivery + redaction notes (FinServCo)

Alex — thanks for confirming on the call this morning. We've uploaded the requested package and included a short narrative you can provide to the assessor. Download link and summary below.

Download (internal staging, one-time link): https://drive.redwood.company/drive/folders/1a2B3cSDLC-pack
Manifest summary (what's included):
- redacted-code-review-samples.zip — three representative PRs. Developer identifiers replaced with uid-hash, PR ids preserved for traceability. Diffs left intact; no secrets present in commits (scanned).
- ci-runner-logs-redacted.pdf — runner step timeline, exit codes, durations. Usernames and IPs redacted; timestamps preserved.
- deploy-ticket-history.csv — mapping of ticket -> PR -> deploy ts -> approver role. Approver names redacted per our customer-requested privacy baseline.
- kms-token-access-snapshot.csv — rotation events for deploy keys (service principals redacted to svc-xxxxx).

Redaction & retention policy (short):
- We redact human identifiers at the request of external assessors but preserve stable artifact identifiers (PR ids, ticket ids) to show end-to-end traceability.
- Audit logs are sampled for the requested window; full logs are retained per our retention policy (90 days for CI traces, 365 days for KMS rotation events) and are available under an NDA if the assessor requires deeper sampling.

If the assessor requires PR ids removed we can re-run mapping and deliver by 2026-11-09 EOD. Otherwise please confirm acceptance and I'll share the HubSpot record id and mark the intake as delivered (HS-12345).

Happy to walk the assessor through artifacts on a 30–45 minute call; suggest Tue 2026-11-09 10:00am PT if that works.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Director, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redacted-code-review-samples.zip (application/zip), ci-runner-logs-redacted.pdf (application/pdf), deploy-ticket-history.csv (text/csv), kms-token-access-snapshot.csv (text/csv)
